_note: CALIBRATION gold set #4 (AppTrail) — labels are Claude's best guess for Robert to CORRECT. Distinct domain from recipebox and from the nine scoring visions. gold_borderline=true marks the deliberate adjacent<->off_domain seam plants. Seam tags in notes: alpha=job-derivable-but-no-citable-phrase (favors audience_goal), beta=broad-phrase-but-off-the-stated-job (stresses off_domain recall), delta=purpose-fit-but-orthogonal-to-every-per-feature-job (expected to stress audience_goal, the reverse failure). No gamma here; delta plays the discriminating third seam.

vision.purpose: A tracker that helps an active job seeker keep every application organized and never miss a follow-up on the applications they already have going.
target_audience: Job seekers running many applications at once who lose track of stages and deadlines
People who want to know the right next step on each application they have open

application_pipeline.description: Tracks each application through stages (applied, screen, interview, offer) on a board the seeker moves cards across.

followup_reminders.description: Reminds the seeker when an application has gone quiet long enough that it is time to follow up.

status_extraction_from_email.description: Reads the seeker's job-related email and updates the matching application's stage automatically (e.g. detecting an interview invite or a rejection).

candidates.name: email_intent_classification
candidates.rough_description: Classifies an incoming job-related email as rejection, interview invite, offer, or other, so the application's stage can be updated.
candidates.note: status_extraction_from_email cannot update the stage without reading the email's intent. Necessity, cite status_extraction_from_email.

candidates.name: email_to_application_threading
candidates.rough_description: Matches each incoming email to the correct application by employer/thread so the right card updates.
candidates.note: status_extraction_from_email must update the matching application; this is necessary to do that correctly. Cite status_extraction_from_email.

candidates.name: quiet_application_timing_model
candidates.rough_description: Decides when an application has gone quiet long enough to warrant a follow-up nudge.
candidates.note: followup_reminders' stated outcome (remind when it is time to follow up) requires this. Necessity, cite followup_reminders.

candidates.name: followup_message_drafting
candidates.rough_description: Drafts a polite follow-up email for an application that has gone quiet, ready for the seeker to send.
candidates.note: Serves the never-miss-a-follow-up purpose; followup_reminders works without it. Enhancement, cite purpose.

candidates.name: interview_prep_reminder_for_scheduled_interview
candidates.rough_description: For an interview already on a tracked application's card, reminds the seeker to prepare beforehand and links their notes for that application.
candidates.note: Tied to a tracked application and the 'right next step' purpose; not required by a feature. Enhancement. (Contrast with the generic practice bank below.)

candidates.name: job_board_scraper
candidates.rough_description: Scrapes external job boards to find and surface new openings matching the seeker's profile.
candidates.note: Discovery of new jobs; the vision is organizing applications the seeker already has open. Different job. Guardrail.

candidates.name: job_seeker_networking_feed
candidates.rough_description: A social feed where job seekers connect, share tips, and post about their search.
candidates.note: Social/community surface; the vision is a personal organizing tool. Guardrail.

candidates.name: generic_interview_question_practice_bank
candidates.rough_description: A large searchable library of common interview questions the seeker can browse and rehearse against, not connected to any specific tracked application.
candidates.note: SEAM (beta): 'job seekers' and 'next step' offer a broad surface a phrase-anchored judge may credit, but this is a standalone study tool tied to no tracked application and serves none of the per-application jobs (track, follow up, auto-update). Proposed off_domain; contestable. Deliberately paired against the application-tied prep reminder above.

candidates.name: per_application_resume_tailoring
candidates.rough_description: For a specific tracked application, suggests tweaks to the seeker's resume to better match that job's posting.
candidates.note: SEAM (alpha): no purpose/audience phrase mentions resumes, so a phrase-anchored judge has little to cite (likely off_domain); but a job derived from application_pipeline (advance a tracked application / know the next step) is plausibly served. Proposed adjacent.

candidates.name: search_wide_stats_dashboard
candidates.rough_description: Shows the seeker aggregate stats across all their applications: response rate, average time-to-interview, and where applications stall.
candidates.note: SEAM (delta): fits the stated purpose (keep the whole search organized; audience runs 'many applications at once') at a cross-application level, but maps to no single per-feature job, each of which is scoped to one application. A phrase-anchored judge should cite the purpose and land adjacent; a job-deriving judge that over-narrows to per-feature jobs may wrongly reject as off_domain. Proposed adjacent; the reverse-direction discriminator.
